feedback: Judged before racing. The candidate is valid and changes only controller.kd (0.2 to 0.25) relative to iteration 3, which kept kp at 4.0. Iteration 3 scored 62.5, below the best raced design (iteration 1, kp 3.0, kd 0.15, score 71.2). Its oscillation rose to 0.21 on the oval, which is the case the earlier feedback rule covers: raise kd before changing kp. The candidate tests that. Iteration 2 showed that raising ki to 0.9 lowered progress on every track, so ki stays at 0.3, and geometry and base_speed 1.3 are unchanged, so the race isolates the damping. The main weakness is that max_error has sat at 0.062 to 0.065 m in every iteration (0 to 3) whatever the gains, so a kd change alone is unlikely to remove the off-track exit. Do not treat the expected outcome in the rationale as established. After the race, decide from the measurements. If steering_oscillation stays under about 0.2 and max_error is still near 0.06 m, the next step is to move the sensors forward to y about 0.06 for earlier look-ahead (a geometry change), or try kp about 5 with the same kd. If progress reaches about 0.995 with no line loss, raise base_speed toward 1.8, since speed is then the binding limit. If the score falls below the iteration 1 best (71.2), return to kp 3.0 and kd 0.15 and make the sensor look-ahead change on that base instead.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation stays under about 0.2 and max_error is still near 0.06 m with line_loss_events of 1 or more, move geometry.sensor_positions forward to y about 0.06 (from 0.04) to test earlier look-ahead, keeping kp and kd as they are. Iteration 3 showed max_error stuck at 0.062 to 0.065 m whatever kp did, so gain changes alone have not moved that floor.

If the race shows progress at or near 0.995 with no line loss, raise controller.base_speed from 1.3 toward 1.8. Iterations 0 to 3 all went off track, so speed matters only once the robot stays on the line.

If the race scores below 71.2 (the iteration 1 best) or oscillation exceeds about 0.2, revert to kp 3.0 and kd 0.15 (iteration 1) and change only the sensor look-ahead, so the test stays isolated against the best raced design.
